unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: After closing, a visitor in a corporate lobby ignores your leave order and swings a backpack at your head. You are unarmed. What is the lawful force path?

options.a: Create space, keep verbal commands, and use only defensive force law and post orders allow
options.b: Throw the first punch so the encounter ends before police can get there tonight
options.c: Announce a citizen's arrest for last week's rumored laptop theft from another floor
options.d: Chase them onto the public street and pin them on the sidewalk as standing house policy tonight

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Unarmed officers work a force continuum of presence, voice, and the minimum physical defense the statute and post orders allow. A backpack swing can justify blocking or a control hold to stop the attack, not a punitive beating, a rumor-based arrest, or a public-road takedown.

distractorExplanations.b: Striking first as a tactic is assault, not a continuum step; force answers an imminent threat, not speed.
distractorExplanations.c: Citizen's arrest needs an offense you can lawfully act on now, not hallway gossip about another night.
distractorExplanations.d: Off-property chases and pins exceed typical unarmed post authority and create crash and false-arrest risk.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: A grocery cashier radios that a shopper 'looks guilty.' You never saw concealment or a pass of the registers. They ask you to make a citizen's arrest. What is required?

options.a: Reasonable suspicion that some crime might have happened somewhere in the store tonight is enough
options.b: An offense committed in your presence, or the exact citizen-arrest rule your state writes
options.c: A supervisor's radio 'go ahead' even when you did not see a crime on camera or in person
options.d: A signed owner complaint handed to you at the podium before you touch anyone at all

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Private guards are not police. Where citizen's arrest exists, it usually requires a crime committed in the officer's presence or another narrow statutory trigger. A cashier's vibe, a boss's permission, or a paper complaint does not create arrest power you personally lack.

distractorExplanations.a: Reasonable suspicion is a police stop idea; it is not the typical private-person arrest threshold.
distractorExplanations.c: A supervisor cannot authorize an arrest the statute does not allow; the legal basis is the crime facts.
distractorExplanations.d: An owner complaint may start a police case later; it does not by itself give a guard arrest authority.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: At a gated apartment courtyard, the manager clearly withdraws consent and tells a guest to leave. The guest stays on the grass. What should the unarmed officer do?

options.a: Block the courtyard gate and hold them until they sign a trespass statement
options.b: Treat it as a civil spat only and refuse to involve police
options.c: Repeat the leave order, document notice, and call police if they will not go
options.d: Wait until a no-trespass sign is bolted at every pedestrian gate before acting

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: After consent is withdrawn, remaining on private property is typically criminal trespass. The unarmed officer's job is notice, documentation, and police if the person will not leave—not a homemade lock-in for a signature, and not waiting for extra signage when verbal notice already happened.

distractorExplanations.a: Holding someone for a signed statement is confinement without a merchant-detention basis and risks false imprisonment.
distractorExplanations.b: Refusing to leave after notice is not merely civil in most states; police routinely take those calls.
distractorExplanations.d: Clear verbal withdrawal of consent is notice; posted signs are another method, not the only one.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: In a jewelry boutique you watch a shopper pocket a pendant, walk past open registers, and push the exit. How should detention work?

options.a: Run a long stockroom interrogation until they confess on your phone video
options.b: Keep them in the office for a fixed hour before anyone calls police
options.c: Stop them on the manager's 'bad vibe' with no observed concealment
options.d: Make a short, documented stop under post orders and shopkeeper rules, then call police

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Merchant/shopkeeper detention, where it exists, is a brief hold based on observed facts that amount to probable cause of theft, then a prompt handoff to police. Unarmed officers are not detectives: no confession theater, no arbitrary hour, and no hunches.

distractorExplanations.a: Extracting a confession exceeds a private detention; questioning for a case belongs to police.
distractorExplanations.b: Reasonable time is fact-specific and short; a preset hour before calling police is not the rule.
distractorExplanations.c: A manager's vibe is not probable cause; you need what you saw: concealment and a pass of the point of sale.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: You hold a trespasser in a warehouse conference room for arriving police. They start volunteering a story. Do you read Miranda?

options.a: No. Miranda is a police custodial-interrogation warning, not a private guard script
options.b: Yes, before you ask even their name or why they are waiting on the dock tonight
options.c: Yes, because a uniformed private officer is treated as a state actor at every stop you make
options.d: Yes, so any later statement they give police will automatically come in at trial

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Miranda attaches to custodial interrogation by government agents. Private unarmed officers generally are not state actors and do not administer those warnings. Your job is a lawful, short detention and a clean handoff—not a recorded interview designed to look like a police booking.

distractorExplanations.b: Asking identity or waiting for police is not a Miranda trigger for a private guard.
distractorExplanations.c: A contractor uniform does not turn you into a sworn officer; state-actor status is the exception, not the default.
distractorExplanations.d: You cannot 'pre-Mirandize' someone to make their later police statement admissible; that is a police/court issue.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: Garage cameras show a window smash from an hour ago. The same person is now at the pay station. You did not see the smash live. Citizen's arrest?

options.a: Yes. Recorded video is legally the same as watching the crime happen in real time
options.b: No. Delayed footage is not 'in your presence'; follow post orders and call police
options.c: Yes, because they are still on the property, which restarts the offense clock tonight
options.d: Yes, so patrol arrives to a finished arrest package you already completed for them

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Citizen's arrest is narrow. Reviewing later video is investigation, not presence. Remaining on site after an hour-old smash does not by itself recreate the offense in your sight. Observe, identify, preserve video, and let police decide—do not invent arrest power from playback.

distractorExplanations.a: Playback helps identification; it is not the statutory 'in your presence' seeing of the crime.
distractorExplanations.c: Being on the lot later is not a new smash you witnessed; do not bootstrap an old felony into a fresh arrest.
distractorExplanations.d: Packaging an arrest you are not authorized to make creates false-arrest liability instead of helping police.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: In a hotel ballroom you take an aggressor to the carpet with a control hold after they shove a guest. No visible injury. When is a use-of-force report due?

options.a: Only if the subject later files a written complaint with the hotel front desk
options.b: Never, if you called police and they will write the official report for the hotel
options.c: This shift, because you put hands on a person, even without a visible injury
options.d: Only when a supervisor later asks you for a written statement about the hold

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Hands-on contact is a reportable use of force on unarmed posts whether or not skin is broken. Write it the same shift while facts are fresh. A later complaint, a police report, or a supervisor's curiosity are not the trigger—the contact is.

distractorExplanations.a: Waiting for a complaint hides force; the duty to document starts when you used it.
distractorExplanations.b: Police paper covers their actions; it does not replace your employer's use-of-force report.
distractorExplanations.d: Mandatory reporting is not optional homework assigned only if a supervisor remembers to ask.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: At a museum bag table a visitor's purse looks bulky. There is no posted bag-check and they did not consent. May you rummage inside?

options.a: Yes. Unarmed officers have the same bag-search power as airport checkpoint staff
options.b: Yes. A museum is public enough that purses lose privacy at the door
options.c: Yes, if you label the rummage a 'medical safety check' and dump the contents
options.d: No, unless consent, a posted lawful bag-check, or a specific retail/event rule applies

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Private security searches rest on consent, condition-of-entry policy the person can refuse by leaving, or a narrow merchant rule—not on a guard card. Inventing TSA power or a medical pretext is a civil search/battery problem. If policy does not authorize it, observe and call a supervisor or police.

distractorExplanations.a: TSA checkpoint authority is federal aviation screening; it does not travel with a private unarmed card.
distractorExplanations.b: Public access to a lobby does not erase purse privacy or create a warrantless dump right.
distractorExplanations.c: Relabeling a search as medical does not create consent or a lawful inspection rule.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: You leave a busy loading dock unmanned for twenty minutes to jump-start a friend's car in visitor parking. A contractor is then hurt by an unattended pallet jack. Where is liability highest?

options.a: Abandoning a foreseeable-risk post you were hired to watch
options.b: Calling 911 for the injury before you notify the shift supervisor
options.c: Writing a factual incident report that a lawyer might later read in court
options.d: Refusing a client request that would have broken written post orders

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Negligence tracks duty, breach, and foreseeability. A dock with moving equipment is a known hazard; leaving it for a personal errand is a classic abandonment claim. Calling 911, writing the truth, and declining illegal orders are protective, not the liability peak.

distractorExplanations.b: Emergency medical notice first is reasonable care; it does not create the injury.
distractorExplanations.c: An accurate report is expected evidence; liability comes from the unmanned dock, not the paperwork.
distractorExplanations.d: Honoring post orders against a bad client ask is compliance, not negligence.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: On a hotel lounge post you see a 19-year-old drinking beer a bartender already poured. What is the unarmed officer's lawful handling?

options.a: Confiscate their ID and keep it at the podium until closing
options.b: Stop the service, document, and notify the manager and police if the license requires it
options.c: Stay out of it because only the bartender can be cited for the sale
options.d: Warn them once and let them finish if they drain the glass quickly

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Licensed alcohol sites make underage possession and service a documented, escalated issue. Security does not punish with pain or keep identity documents. Stopping the drink, writing what you saw, and bringing the manager (and police when the permit or house rule requires) is the lane.

distractorExplanations.a: You may refuse entry or service; retaining someone's ID is not a typical unarmed power and looks like theft/coercion.
distractorExplanations.c: Security on a licensed floor shares the duty to stop and report; it is not bartender-only.
distractorExplanations.d: Letting the minor finish continues the violation and the license risk.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: At a data-center lobby you overhear a visitor's door codes and a planned network shutdown. What may you do with that information?

options.a: Share it after you quit, because the job's confidentiality ends with the last shift
options.b: Tell friends the story if you leave the company and employee names out
options.c: Keep it off social media and off-duty talk; the client owns that operational detail
options.d: Treat it as public once you clock out, because the lobby is a semi-public space

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Codes, outage windows, and similar client operations are confidential whether you are on the clock or not. Duty usually survives the job. Stripping names does not anonymize a unique site. Lobby access for screening is not a license to republish secrets.

distractorExplanations.a: NDAs and common-law duties typically outlast employment; quitting is not a disclosure switch.
distractorExplanations.b: Details alone identify the site and the risk; omitting names is not a safe harbor.
distractorExplanations.d: End of shift does not publish the information; semi-public entry is still a controlled client space.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: On a stadium concourse a fan insults you. No crime is in progress. A supervisor radios 'grab him and drag him to command.' What is lawful?

options.a: Decline. Mouthing off is not a basis to seize someone; detention needs a lawful ground
options.b: Drag them, because a supervisor's radio order is itself enough arrest authority tonight
options.c: Cuff them 'for attitude' until they apologize at the command post in front of guests
options.d: Walk them to the public sidewalk and hold them there without a stated offense

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Detain and arrest are not the same, and neither is a tool for hurt feelings. Unarmed officers need a statute, merchant rule, or imminent threat—not a radio dare. A supervisor cannot manufacture probable cause. Document the insult, ask them to leave if house rules allow, and call police for real crimes.

distractorExplanations.b: Chain of command does not override false-imprisonment law; illegal orders are refused and reported.
distractorExplanations.c: Attitude is not an offense; cuffs without a lawful detention are a seizure you cannot justify.
distractorExplanations.d: Moving the hold off property does not legalize confinement without cause.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: At a gym you suspect a member stole towels but you saw nothing. They head for the only exit and you stand in the doorway with arms out. What legal risk is that?

options.a: None, if you smile and call it 'waiting for cameras' instead of calling it a detention
options.b: False imprisonment, because you blocked the only exit with no legal basis to confine
options.c: None, because asking any trespasser to leave is the same act as blocking a door
options.d: False imprisonment even if you later only follow them at a distance in the parking lot

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: False imprisonment is unlawful confinement—blocking the sole exit so a person reasonably believes they cannot leave. Suspicion without observed facts is not shopkeeper detention. A polite label does not change the barrier. Asking someone to leave, or watching from a distance, is not the same as a human gate.

distractorExplanations.a: Relabeling a blocked door as a camera wait still confines; intent-to-be-nice is not a defense.
distractorExplanations.c: A leave order restricts no movement; a barred doorway does. Those are different acts.
distractorExplanations.d: Open-air surveillance without boxing them in is generally not confinement.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: A property manager hands you a stack of eviction notices and tells you to serve tenants on tonight's unarmed tower post. What is true?

options.a: Your guard card already covers process serving, lockouts, and paper drops
options.b: Mobile patrol always includes serving legal papers between client sites at night
options.c: Serving process is outside the unarmed guard role and needs its own authority
options.d: Post orders can add process-server powers the license never granted on this post

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: Unarmed officers observe, report, control access, and detain only where law and post orders allow. Serving process, executing lockouts, or acting as a bail recovery agent are separate occupations and often separate licenses. A client memo cannot mint that authority.

distractorExplanations.a: A typical guard registration is not a process-server or sheriff's deputy credential.
distractorExplanations.b: Patrol checks client properties; it is not a courier job for lawsuits or evictions.
distractorExplanations.d: Post orders allocate site tasks; they cannot expand statutory power the card lacks.

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.prompt: On a nightclub sidewalk two patrons are trading punches. Post orders say observe, report, and do not wade into active fights. You are unarmed. Best action?

options.a: Step between them with your own strikes so the fight ends faster
options.b: Tackle both into the street to keep the doorway clear for paying guests
options.c: Ignore the fight entirely, including radio and 911, until a manager arrives
options.d: Create distance, radio, call police, and use force only if an innocent person is imminently attacked

unarmed-security-officer-readiness-check.explanation: The unarmed continuum starts at presence and communication, not entering a two-person brawl. Post orders that forbid fight entry are lawful limits. You still summon help. Physical force is reserved for an imminent attack on you or someone you may defend—not to 'win' the fight or clear a door by dumping people into traffic.

distractorExplanations.a: Joining with strikes makes you a combatant and exceeds observe-and-report orders.
distractorExplanations.b: A street tackle is new force, new crash risk, and not a trespass or detention solution.
distractorExplanations.c: Observe-and-report still requires radio and police; silence is neglect of the post.
